metadata.name: jury-unanimous
metadata.description: Three jurors, one arson case, up to three sealed ballots. Each juror noticed a different detail in the exhibits, so none of them can reach a just verdict alone. The foreperson runs the ballots, reports only the split, and records the jury's verdict — unanimous, or hung.
metadata.author: bearpit

goals: Jurors: pool what each of you noticed, argue it honestly, and seal a ballot every round — unanimity or a hung jury, never a lazy verdict.
Foreperson: run the ballots, report only the split, and record the jury's verdict with rule().
spec.guidelines:
THE CASE — State v. Merrick Vance, arson of the Harborview warehouse on the night of 14 March.
THE CHARGE: that Vance set fire to his own warehouse to collect on the stock insured inside. The fire began at about 00:01.

THE PROSECUTION'S EVIDENCE:
  P1. The access log shows a Vance company keycard opened the loading door at 23:41 — twenty minutes before the fire.
  P2. Eleven days before the fire, Vance signed a policy raising the cover on the stock from $150,000 to $400,000.
  P3. Dolan, the night clerk across the street, saw a man of Vance's build leave by the alley at 23:55.

THE DEFENCE'S EVIDENCE:
  D1. Vance reported a keycard LOST on 11 March and was issued a replacement.
  D2. The fire marshal placed the ignition point at the wiring cabinet, which is on the building's known-faulty list.
  D3. Dolan watched from 40 metres, at night, in rain, and admits he never saw the man's face.

THE STANDARD: convict ONLY if guilt is proved BEYOND REASONABLE DOUBT. If a reasonable doubt remains, the verdict is not-guilty.

Each juror also noticed ONE detail in the exhibits that the other two missed — it is in your own brief. Deliberation is worth nothing unless you put it on the table.

HOW THE BALLOTS WORK. The jury room is turn-based: you hold the floor for exactly ONE message per round, and there are at most THREE ballots. THE BALLOT NUMBER IS THE ROUND NUMBER (round 1 = ballot-1, round 2 = ballot-2, round 3 = ballot-3); call turn_status() if you are unsure which round you are in.
On your turn: (1) answer the argument made before yours and say where you now stand; (2) seal your ballot — MANDATORY, every round — with
    submit_sealed(round='ballot-<N>', payload='guilty')
  or
    submit_sealed(round='ballot-<N>', payload='not-guilty')
The payload is EXACTLY one of those two lowercase tokens: no prose, no prefix, no 'VERDICT:', no capitals, no full stop. Anything else is counted as a different vote and can hang the jury by accident.
Ballots are sealed and revealed together, so there is no bandwagon to join. The foreperson reports only the SPLIT (e.g. '2-1'), never who voted which way. You may change your mind BETWEEN ballots; a ballot you have already sealed can never be changed.
The foreperson does not deliberate and does not vote. Only the foreperson's rule() call ends the trial.
spec.restrictions: Do not invent evidence: the exhibits are exactly the guidelines above plus the one detail in your own brief. Do not post a ballot as a chat line instead of sealing it — an unsealed 'vote' counts for nothing. Do not use the 🏁 character in any message: it is reserved for the foreperson's closing line.
